messages:
phil: Heads-up — Acme legal sent over an enterprise SQ asking for KMS key provenance, RBAC change logs, and an incident response runbook. Meeting in 30 to go over gaps.
anya: copying the SQ here: they want key creation timestamps, key rotation policy, KMS access principal list, and proof of rotation events for the last 12 months. also ask for sample exported audit logs.
sana: can we provide that without exporting unredacted tenant data?
oscar: yes — we can produce KMS admin event slices and rotate-proof artifacts. Steps: 1) export CloudKMS Admin Audit events where protoPayload.methodName = \"cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.update\" or \"google.iam.admin.v1.SetIamPolicy\" 2) redact resource names for customer-owned keys unless they gave consent.
beth: for the runbook piece they specifically want: who gets paged, proof of containment, timeline format, and how we notify customers. do we have a canonical doc?
phil: we have a draft IR runbook in Confluence but it's a bit productized. need a customer-facing, redacted version.
anya: quick Q on RBAC: Acme asked for a change history for roles mapping -> who changed org-level roles for KMS (create/update) in last 18 months. We store that in internal audit logs?
oscar: yes — org-admin changes are recorded in our admin-audit logs. query example: 
```
resource.type=\"project\"
logName=\"projects/redwood-prod/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Factivity\"
protoPayload.methodName=(\"SetIamPolicy\" OR \"CreateRole\" OR \"UpdateRole\")
protoPayload.serviceName: \"cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com\"
timestamp>=\"2024-03-01T00:00:00Z\"
```
phil: nice. include who approved via metadata annotation if present.
sana: vuln triage aside — we discovered yesterday a medium vuln in dependency xyz that exposed API token metadata to logs. incident triage notes?
beth: triage update: flagged as mav-2026-044, MLR assigned, mitigation = scrub token patterns from logs and rotate affected tokens. Impact: one customer test tenant; no production tokens exposed.
anya: can we reconcile that with Acme's ask about historic audit logs? they want assurance logs weren't leaked. how to prove?
oscar: we can provide a signed statement plus filtered log extracts showing no token strings present after scrub time. also provide pre-scrub vs post-scrub counts of matched regex hits.
phil: add brief timeline: discovery -> containment -> rotate -> audit -> notify. Acme expects dates + owners.
beth: for KMS key rotation proof — we can supply keyVersion state snapshots and signed access logs. sample key policy snippet to include: 
```
{
  \"bindings\": [
    {\"role\":\"roles/cloudkms.admin\",\"members\":[\"serviceAccount:redwood-kms-admin@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com\"]}
  ],
  \"rotationPeriod\":\"7776000s\" // 90 days
}
```
anya: need to be careful with exact service account names — redact to sa:REDACTED where appropriate.
sana: what about delivering audit logs? they asked for syslog/ELK exports — we can generate a gzipped tar of filtered events. Any compliance approval needed?
oscar: must run through compliance export playbook (we have an internal step that does PII scan + legal signoff). I'll kick that off.
sec-bot: Reminder: export workflow requires two approvers from security + one from legal. Use /exports create --project redwood-prod --filter \"protoPayload.methodName:\\"SetIamPolicy\\"\" --range \"2024-01-01..2025-01-01\"
phil: ok. action items: oscar to produce example query and run PII scan (due EOD tomorrow), beth to draft customer-friendly IR timeline + notify wording (due monday), anya to prepare redacted KMS rotation artifacts (due monday), sana to capture vuln triage note for SQ attachment. I'll run the call with Acme on Wed 11am PT.
beth: also prepare a short FAQ: \"How do you limit who can rotate keys? How do you detect unauthorized rotations?\" small bullets.
oscar: note — if they push for HSM attestation, we need to surface limitations: hosted offering uses cloud KMS; Dedicated/private can use customer HSMs but attestation collection differs.
anya: ack. I'll map that into the responses.
sana: +1. Anything else?
oscar: one more — Acme asked about SIEM ingest of audit logs in their tenant. We support export to their Splunk via Pub/Sub -> Forwarder, but we need network details. product provided template earlier.
phil: we'll attach the Splunk forwarding template and an example IAM allowlist. good work team.
beth: :thumbsup:
phil: meeting pinned in calendar. thanks everyone.
